text: use BigSur, first create Seurat object containing raw transcript counts gene. preprocessing step, ensure genes zero counts across cells. {r} library(BigSur) example.seurat <- CreateSeuratObject(data, min.cells=1) Pass object BigSur function desired parameters. parameters follows: - seurat.obj: Seurat object containing raw transcript counts filtered zero count genes. - assay: Assay slot containing raw transcript counts (default “RNA”). - counts.slot: Slot within assay containing raw counts matrix (default “counts”). - cv.est.method: String. Sets method used determining coefficient variation used define null distributions. three options : 1) “Single”: Determines scalar value c. 2) “MeanSpecific”: Estimates relationship mean expression expected coefficient variation predicts null value gene. 3)“TwoComponent”: Estimates relationship mean expression expected coefficient variation using two parameter fit. - null.distribution: String. Sets null distribution estimate p-values Fano factors correlations. “NB”: Negative binomial, “PLN”: Poisson log-normal. (Defaults negative binomial.) - variable.features: Boolean. true, BigSur identify select variable features based modified corrected Fano factor. (Default true) - correlations:Boolean. true, BigSur identify statistically significant gene-gene correlations. (Default false) - first.pass.cutoff: Integer. Removes roots p-value calculations root Abs[Sqrt(2)*InverseErfc(2*10^-first.pass.cutoff)]. higher number, correlations removed initial screening. - inverse.fano.moments: Boolean. true, BigSur calculate moments inverse Fano factor pairs performing Cornish Fisher expansion. Setting false significantly speed calculation cost accuracy. - fano.alpha: Double. Desired false discovery cutoff labeling variable features. (Default 0.05). - min.fano: Double. Minimum mcFano value considered variable genes. - cor.alpha: Double. Desired false discovery cutoff labeling statistically significant correlations. - log.file: Boolean. true, log file created. - log.file.dir: String. Path desired location log file. *Note: Default string set work Unix based file structures (.e., manually set Windows). example, calculate highly variable features significant correlations dataset default false discovery cutoffs use: {r} example.output <- BigSur(example.seurat, variable.feature=T, correlations=T) function return new Seurat object following attachments: variable.features == True: -Modified corrected Fano factors (mcfanos) respective adjusted (Benjamini Hochberg) p values stored assay’s @meta.data slot. highly variable features boolean vector stored typical slot used FindVariableFeatures. correlations == True: -Modified corrected Pearson correlation coefficients respective adjusted (Benjamini Hochberg) p values (log10 format) stored @misc slot. Regardless parameters: -eta theta parameter values used estimate per-gene value null coefficient variation stored @misc slot. -modified corrected Pearson residuals matrix stored assay’s $data slot.
